title: Section 1 Overview
content:
HawkVision AI is an enterprise-grade artificial intelligence visual safety and operational monitoring
system tailored for industrial, manufacturing, logistics, and heavy commercial environments. The
platform transforms existing video camera networks IP/RTSP) into real-time safety, security, and
operational intelligence sensors using deep learning at the edge and centralized cloud analytics.

title: Supported Safety Usecases
content:
●
Intrusion & Exclusion Zone Detection: Identifies unauthorized personnel entering
restricted areas, active heavy machinery paths, or dangerous operational zones. Supports
time-scheduled rules and spatial sub-zoning.
●
PPE Compliance Monitoring: Automatically verifies compliance with Personal Protective
Equipment requirements, specifically detecting Hardhats, High-Visibility Vests, and Safety
Glasses.
●
Vehicle Speeding & Logistics Control: Measures real-time speed of forklifts, AGVs,
semi-trucks, and yard vehicles across warehouse aisles, logistics yards, and pedestrian
walkways.
●
Near-Miss Identification: Uses spatial trajectory modeling to detect near-collisions
between machinery/vehicles and ground personnel, enabling preventive intervention before
actual incidents occur.
●
Fire & Smoke Detection: Applies specialized vision models to identify early-stage flame
ignition and smoke plumes in indoor facilities, chemical storage areas, and open yards
faster than traditional thermal/particle sensors.

title: Core Design Principles
content:
●
Distributed Edge Computing: All computer vision inference, frame decoding, and spatial
analysis occur locally on dedicated hardware nodes deployed at each facility site. Raw
video streams never leave the local network, saving bandwidth and enforcing privacy.
●
Ultra-Low Latency Alerting: Edge-level detection processes frame data in under 100
milliseconds, routing critical alerts immediately to site safety coordinators via push
notifications, webhooks, or local sirens.
●
Multi-Tenant Hierarchy: Features strict multi-level tenancy Customer $\rightarrow$ Site
$\rightarrow$ Camera $\rightarrow$ ROI) supporting granular access controls, global
multi-site management, and isolated compute boundaries.
●
Automated Alert Routing & Triage: Incident payloads containing annotated frames,
metadata, and severity indexes are automatically categorized, delivered to site shift
personnel, and monitored through a lifecycle tracking system.
●
Audit Compliance & Historical Safety Analytics: Stores structured incident metadata and
visual proofs to support OSHA, ISO 45001, and corporate EHS audit requirements, driving
continuous risk mitigation strategies.

title: Tier 1: Customer
content:
The top-level entity representing the enterprise organization (e.g., Global Logistics Corp).
●
Controls global organizational settings, enterprise billing schedules, and master retention
policies.
●
Manages global administrator permissions (HawkVision Admin, Org Admin).
●
Serves as the top-level isolation boundary for data tenancy, analytics aggregation, and
license enforcement.

title: Tier 2: Site
content:
Represents a distinct physical building, campus, manufacturing plant, or fulfillment center (e.g.,
Austin Assembly Plant #4).
●
Shift Configuration: Defines local operational shifts (e.g., Shift A - Day, Shift B -
Night, 24∕7 Operations). Incident logging and notification routing map directly to active
shift schedules.
●
Site Functional Tags: Holds the site-wide repository of Functional Tags tailored to local
operational zones.
●
Edge Machine Association: Links directly to local site hardware Edge Node Appliance).
Each site maintains a persistent sync connection with its edge machine.

title: Tier 3: Camera
content:
Represents an individual physical visual sensor connected to the site network via RTSP Real-Time
Streaming Protocol) or ONVIF protocols.
●
Holds stream parameters: RTSP URL, resolution, target frame rate FPS, network
credentials, and stream health metrics.
●
Contains one or more spatial Regions of Interest ROIs.
●
Houses the localized camera execution state Online, Offline, Degraded).

title: Functional Tag Mechanism
content:
Functional Tags serve as the core logical bridge between spatial camera regions and AI detection
rules. Instead of manually binding computer vision models and threshold parameters directly to
every individual camera frame, system administrators assign standardized operational
classifications via Functional Tags.
●
Definition: A Functional Tag represents a standardized zone type within an enterprise (e.g.,
Forklift Aisle, Pedestrian Walkway, Chemical Storage Area, Loading Dock).
●
Rule Mapping: Specific AI Usecases (e.g., Vehicle Speeding Detection, PPE
Verification, Fire & Smoke) are attached to a Functional Tag alongside operational
thresholds (e.g., speed_limit: 15km∕h, required_ppe: ["hardhat", "vest"]).
●
Execution Linkage: When an operator draws an ROI polygon on a camera feed and assigns
a Functional Tag to it, the ROI automatically inherits all AI detection rules tied to that tag.

title: Home Tab Dashboard & Analytics)
content:
The Home Tab provides high-level visualization, operational telemetry, and incident aggregation
across organizational levels.
Custom Dashboards & Layout Customization
Users can build role-based layouts by adding, resizing, and arranging modular widgets:
●
Incident Totals Metric Cards: Real-time counts of total, critical, and unreviewed incidents
across chosen sites.
●
Live Alert Ticker: A real-time, streaming list of incoming edge detection events with instant
preview thumbnails.
●
Severity Distribution Pie Charts: Categorization of events into Low, Medium, High, and
Critical SIF  Serious Injury & Fatality) risk levels.
●
Site Comparison Bar Graphs: Benchmark incident rates across different physical facilities
to target safety training.
●
Time-Series Incident Trends: Line charts showing safety trends over hours, days, weeks,
or shifts.
Global Filter Bar
The Home Tab features a persistent multi-parameter filter bar that dynamically updates all
rendered dashboard widgets:
●
Site: Select all sites, a single campus, or custom site groups.
●
Camera: Filter down to specific visual sensors.
●
Date & Time Range: Absolute (custom calendar picker) or relative (Last 1 Hour, Shift
to Date, Last 30 Days).
●
Shift: Filter by defined operational schedules (Shift A, Shift B, Night Shift).
●
Severity Level: Multi-select options (Low, Medium, High, Critical).
●
Usecase Type (uctype): Filter by AI module (PPE, Speeding, Fire, Intrusion,
Near-Miss).
●
Functional Tags: Filter metrics by operational area types (e.g., all Loading Dock zones
across the enterprise).

title: Configuration Tab Sites, Cameras, ROIs, & Functional Tags)
content:
The Configuration Tab serves as the central management engine for facility setup, spatial camera
mapping, and rule definitions.
Site Management List
●
Displays all configured sites within the customer organization.
●
Shows connection status of edge nodes, connected camera counts, active shift profiles,
and assigned location tags.
Functional Tags Sub-Tab
●
Creation & Editing: Administrators define global or site-specific tags (e.g., Hazardous
Material Zone).
●
Default Usecase Assignment: Select default AI detection rules and parameter values (e.g.,
confidence thresholds, speed limits) tied to each tag.
Cameras Sub-Tab
●
Lists all physical cameras linked to the selected site.
●
Status Monitoring: Tracks sensor state using three indicators:
○
Online: Stream active, decoding normally at target FPS.
○
Offline: Stream unreachable or RTSP connection dropped.
○
Degraded: High frame drop rate, low lighting, camera obstruction, or severe
latency.
Camera ROI & Usecase Configuration Workflow
Setting up visual detection on a camera follows a structured four-step
workflow:┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐

│ Draw custom polygon/rectangle over the live camera feed. │
└────────────────────────────┬─────────────────────────────┘
│

└────────────────────────────┬─────────────────────────────┘
│
▼

│
▼

└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
1.
Draw Region of Interest ROIOpen the camera setup view. Use the polygon or rectangle
drawing tool to mark specific spatial boundaries on the live camera canvas.
2.
Assign Functional Tag: Select a pre-configured Functional Tag from the dropdown list to
apply to the newly created ROI.
3.
Dynamic Rule Fetching: The UI automatically fetches and displays all default AI usecases
and default detection thresholds tied to that tag.
4.
Fine-tune & Save Rules: The operator can customize sensitivity settings, adjust thresholds,
enable or disable specific usecases for this camera ROI, or remove existing rule
assignments.

title: Site Edge Sync Mechanism & Technical Pipeline
content:
Configuration changes made in the Cloud Web Application do not automatically disrupt live edge
processing. They must be explicitly deployed using the Site Edge Sync mechanism.
Sync Button Functionality
Located in the header of every Site Configuration page. It turns amber whenever un-synced
configuration changes exist (e.g., new ROIs drawn, camera added, tag modified). Clicking Sync
initiates an atomic configuration push to the physical edge appliance deployed at that specific site.
End-to-End Sync Lifecycle
┌──────────────┐          ┌──────────────────────┐          ┌──────────────────────┐
┌──────────────────────┐
│ Web UI Sync  │─────────>│ Central Cloud        │─────────>│ Site Edge Machine
│─────────>│ Local Stream         │
│ Triggered    │          │ Backend Packaging)  │ Payload)│ Engine Reload      │          │ Processors
Updated   │
└──────────────┘          └──────────────────────┘          └──────────────────────┘
└──────────────────────┘
1.
Trigger: User clicks Sync to Edge on the site configuration page.
2.
Packaging: Central cloud backend compiles a unified JSON manifest containing site
configurations, camera manifests, ROI coordinates, and active model parameters.
3.
Payload Delivery: Cloud backend pushes the JSON payload over a secure WebSocket/TLS
channel to the local Site Edge Machine.
4.
Edge Processing Reload: Edge service parses the payload, updates local pipeline configs,
updates local ROI spatial bounding masks, reloads active detection models, and resumes
RTSP stream processing without dropping existing network streams.
Detailed Sync Payload Structure
The configuration package contains the following structure:
●
Site Identifiers & Metadata: site_id, site_name, customer_id, timestamp.
●
Camera Manifest: camera_id, camera_name, stream_url, resolution, fps.
●
ROI Mapping: roi_id, coordinate point arrays [[x1, y1], [x2, y2], ...], assigned
functional_tag_id.
●
Attached Usecase Configurations: usecase_id, usecase_type,
confidence_thresholds, speed limit triggers, bounding parameters.
●
Rulebook & Shift Metadata: Local operational shift schedules, notification escalation
contacts, and severity scoring indices.
Edge-to-Backend Event Delivery Pipeline
1.
Video Decoding & Frame Capture: Local edge machine ingests RTSP video streams from
site cameras.
2.
Local AI Inference Engine: Hardware acceleration passes frames through object detection,
tracking, and spatial ROI mask algorithms.
3.
Violation Detection: If an object (e.g., forklift without driver hardhat, speeding vehicle)
crosses an ROI and breaks an active rule, an event is generated.
4.
Event Payload Construction: Local edge machine builds an event package with bounding
boxes, metric scores (e.g., speed), cropped snapshot images, and metadata.
5.
Event Transmission: Edge machine securely transmits the light payload JSON + cropped
annotated image frame) back to the Cloud Backend Event Table.

●
Annotated Image Snapshot: Displays the frame captured at the exact moment of
detection. Color-coded bounding boxes outline the offending object, person, or vehicle
along with text labels (e.g., NO-Vest, speed: 41 km∕h).
●
Metadata Review Panel: Summarizes critical information: Risk Detected, Site Name,
Camera Name, Created Time, Received Time, Risk Type, Detailed Parameters, SIF Index
score, and active Rulebook.
●
Event Status State Machine:
○
Logged: The default state automatically assigned when an incident payload is
created by the edge and saved to the backend database.
○
Seen: The system automatically updates the event status from Logged to Seen as
soon as an authorized user opens the Event Details Modal.
○
Invalid: If a safety officer determines the alert was a false positive, clicking the
Mark Invalid button transitions the status to Invalid, excluding it from official
safety violation metrics.
